rule.sl:
**have** + stvar + deležnik pomeni, da to zate naredi nekdo drug: **I had my hair cut.** ({m:Dal|f:Dala} sem si postriči lase.) **Mrs Birkett had the roof mended.** Če narediš {m:sam|f:sama}: **I cut my hair.**

Spremeni se le have: **We're having the roof mended.** **We've had the roof mended.** **We'll have the roof mended.** Vprašanje in zanikanje kot pri vsakem glagolu: **Did you have your hair cut?** **I didn't have it done.**

V govoru je pogosto **get**: **I got my hair cut.** **I'm getting the van fixed.** **Get your hair cut!**

Pazi na vrstni red: **I had my hair cut.** (nekdo drug) ni **I had cut my hair.** ({m:sam|f:sama}, še prej). Stvar stoji v sredini, za njo deležnik: **I had the gate mended.**

Kdo: **by**: **We had the gate mended by Mr Dixon.** Z osebo: **I'll get Jack to look at it.** ali **I'll have Jack look at it.**

Ista oblika pove tudi kaj slabega, česar nisi {m:hotel|f:hotela}: **Old Wilf had his wallet stolen on the bus.** **Sam had his van broken into.**
rule.de:
**have** + Sache + Partizip heißt, dass jemand anderer es für dich macht: **I had my hair cut.** (Ich habe mir die Haare schneiden lassen.) **Mrs Birkett had the roof mended.** Machst du es selbst: **I cut my hair.**

Nur have ändert sich: **We're having the roof mended.** **We've had the roof mended.** **We'll have the roof mended.** Frage und Verneinung wie bei jedem Verb: **Did you have your hair cut?** **I didn't have it done.**

Gesprochen ist **get** häufig: **I got my hair cut.** **I'm getting the van fixed.** **Get your hair cut!**

Achte auf die Reihenfolge: **I had my hair cut.** (jemand anderer) ist nicht **I had cut my hair.** (selbst, schon vorher). Die Sache steht in der Mitte, danach das Partizip: **I had the gate mended.** *lassen* ist hier nie *let*.

Wer: **by**: **We had the gate mended by Mr Dixon.** Mit einer Person: **I'll get Jack to look at it.** oder **I'll have Jack look at it.**

Dieselbe Form sagt auch etwas Schlimmes, das du nicht wolltest: **Old Wilf had his wallet stolen on the bus.** **Sam had his van broken into.**
rule.it:
**have** + cosa + participio vuol dire che lo fa un altro per te: **I had my hair cut.** (Mi sono fatt{m:o|f:a} tagliare i capelli.) **Mrs Birkett had the roof mended.** Se lo fai da sol{m:o|f:a}: **I cut my hair.**

Cambia solo have: **We're having the roof mended.** **We've had the roof mended.** **We'll have the roof mended.** Domanda e negazione come per ogni verbo: **Did you have your hair cut?** **I didn't have it done.**

A voce è comune **get**: **I got my hair cut.** **I'm getting the van fixed.** **Get your hair cut!**

Attent{m:o|f:a} all'ordine: **I had my hair cut.** (un altro) non è **I had cut my hair.** (da sol{m:o|f:a}, già prima). La cosa sta in mezzo, poi il participio: **I had the gate mended.** Qui *fare* non è *make*.

Chi: **by**: **We had the gate mended by Mr Dixon.** Con una persona: **I'll get Jack to look at it.** o **I'll have Jack look at it.**

La stessa forma dice anche qualcosa di brutto che non volevi: **Old Wilf had his wallet stolen on the bus.** **Sam had his van broken into.**
rule.en:
**have** + thing + the participle means someone else does it for you: **I had my hair cut.** **Mrs Birkett had the roof mended.** If you do it yourself: **I cut my hair.**

Only have changes: **We're having the roof mended.** **We've had the roof mended.** **We'll have the roof mended.** Questions and no as with any verb: **Did you have your hair cut?** **I didn't have it done.**

In talk **get** is common: **I got my hair cut.** **I'm getting the van fixed.** **Get your hair cut!**

Mind the order: **I had my hair cut.** (someone else) isn't **I had cut my hair.** (myself, earlier). The thing stands in the middle, then the participle: **I had the gate mended** (never *I had the gate mend*).

Who: **by**: **We had the gate mended by Mr Dixon.** With a person: **I'll get Jack to look at it.** or **I'll have Jack look at it.**

The same form says something bad you didn't want: **Old Wilf had his wallet stolen on the bus.** **Sam had his van broken into.**
